questions.q: Why do you usually pass index=False to df.to_csv(...)?
options: Without it, the file is written in the wrong encoding
Without it, pandas writes the row numbers as an extra unnamed column
questions.explain: By default the DataFrame's index is written as the first column; reading the file back then shows an 'Unnamed: 0' column.

questions.q: A European CSV uses semicolons as delimiters and writes 1,5 for 1.5. Which call reads it correctly?
questions.explain: sep sets the field delimiter and decimal sets the decimal-mark character.

questions.q: After pd.read_csv("orders.csv"), the order_date column has dtype object. How do you get real dates?
options: Nothing can be done; CSV files cannot hold dates
Pass parse_dates=["order_date"] to read_csv (or convert with pd.to_datetime afterward)
questions.explain: CSV stores only text, so pandas leaves date columns as strings unless you request parsing.

questions.q: pd.read_excel("orders.xlsx") raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openpyxl'. What is the fix?
options: Install the helper library with pip install openpyxl
questions.explain: pandas relies on an engine library such as openpyxl to read and write .xlsx files, and it must be installed separately.

questions.q: Each order in a JSON file has an items list. Which call produces one row per item while carrying the order id onto each row?
questions.explain: record_path chooses the nested list to expand into rows and meta lists parent fields to repeat on each row.
